newsitem.title: FINLAND: Lively Helsinki climbs on strong Nokia, Merita.
newsitem.headline: Lively Helsinki climbs on strong Nokia, Merita.

text.p: Shares posted strong gains in fairly lively trade on Friday, with bullish Nokia and Merita in the lead and with Europe-wide strength in the wake of Wall Street's Thursday rally giving a further boost, brokers said.
The HEX index climbed 0.92 percent to 2244.83. Volume was fair at 381 million markka.
"It was a Nokia day," one broker said. "There was strength all across Europe," said another.
The telecom share closed at 224.50 markka, up 4.50, after easing off a new calendar-year high of 225.00 markka.
Brokers said Nokia, which accounted for about a third of total bourse volume, rose on expections of a good third-quarter result and on the back of gains in U.S. tech stocks.

A Reuters poll of analysts covering Nokia, published during the session, showed a median forecast for a nine-month profit before tax and minorities of 2.2 billion markka in a range of 2.01-2.43 billion markka.
Nokia is due to report third-quarter results on November 14, and brokers said the interim result would be the focal point next week.
Merita's preferential B share gained 0.70 markka to end at 15.50 after posting a calendar-year high of 15.60 in lively trade, while the usually more liquid Merita A ended flat at 13.90 markka.
Brokers said demand for Merita B was fed by the banking group's announcement on Thursday that it aims to pay a dividend -- the first in five years -- at least on its B shares.
A minor recovery in forestries, which have long been slumping, gave further breadth to the market's rise.
Europe's largest forestry concern, UPM-Kymmene, rose 1.00 markka to close at 88.00.
But one broker called UPM's rise "a technical rebound," and said the share was likely to continue its downward trend if the bad news from the forest industry persists -- as he expected.
Wholesale and retail group Kesko extended losses, falling 1.70 markka to 65.00, on continued uncertainty over EU approval of Kesko's merger with former rival Tuko, brokers said.
